title: PRD update: Regression-aware rollout gates for KV-cache regeneration and tail-latency
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Update the runtime PRD to add deterministic, regression-aware rollout gates that incorporate KV-cache regeneration metrics and tail-latency percentiles. This ticket translates postmortem action items from the KV cache incident into concrete requirements, rollout constraints, and acceptance tests so future deploys do not cause large-scale regeneration cascades or prolonged p99 degradation.
background: During the most recent KV-cache incident, a model rollout triggered concurrent cache invalidations leading to high regen pressure, elevated p95/p99 latencies, and a broad degradation in throughput. Postmortem recommended explicit rollout gates, synthetic verification of KV-cache regen times, and a measurable degradation budget tied to SLOs. Current PRD lacks deterministic checks that tie regression signals to automatic canary rollback and manual abort criteria.
proposed_solution: Add a new PRD section titled 'Regression-Aware Rollout Gates' with: 1) quantitative gate thresholds for KV-cache regen time, tail latency, and error rate; 2) automated synthetic checks executed as part of pre-rollout canary jobs; 3) enforceable abort/rollback criteria and required manual approvals when gates are breached; 4) integration points with runbooks, console alerts, and rollout automation so engineering and on-call can observe, abort, or expedite autorepair.
acceptance_criteria: PRD contains clear numeric thresholds for KV-cache regen median and 95th/99th percentile regeneration time that must be met by canary; thresholds expressed as both absolute ms values and relative regressions versus baseline.

PRD defines tail-latency SLO gates (p95 and p99) and a degradation budget (percentage of requests allowed at degraded latency) that are evaluated during canary and for the first 30 minutes of rollout.
Automated pre-rollout synthetic job blueprint added to PRD describing workload shape, prompt sets, KV-cache warm path, and pass/fail criteria; job is runnable by CI and Console presubmit pipelines.
PRD specifies exact abort actions and owner handoffs: automatic rollback on sustained gate breach for >2m, immediate on-call notification, and mandatory post-rollback incident task creation.
Runbook link and console dashboard panels to surface KV-cache regen distribution and tail-latency histograms are listed in PRD and marked required for release readiness.

Acceptance tests are recorded as runnable test cases: canary synthetic run, induced-cache-regen simulation, and automated verification of rollback behavior; tests pass in CI before merge to main branch.
Operator UX: PRD includes the exact set of console controls (abort, pause, expedite autorepair) and required audit log entries for every manual action during rollout.
A small staged rollout experiment plan is included in PRD to validate gates over multiple model sizes and traffic mixes within the next release window.
tasks: Draft PRD section and circulate to Eng/Infra/Oncall for review
Define numeric thresholds using historical KV-cache incident telemetry (ENG-31821)
Prototype synthetic canary job and add to CI (ENG-31904)
Add console dashboard tiles and alert rules for gate breaches
Document runbook steps and tie to rollback automation
Run canary experiments across 3 model families and capture results
Finalize PRD, get PM/Eng/Design signoff and attach to release criteria
notes: Focus on deterministic, measurable gates that are practical for the on-call flow. Where thresholds are uncertain, PRD should require a short measurement spike experiment before release. Coordinate with Dedicated and Private deployment leads to ensure gates are applicable to reserved pools and air-gapped environments.
